idiom_name: trait port + case-class models + Either-based conversion functions (opaque types for validated ids)
implementation_notes: Scala keeps the boundary in the type system: the domain declares a trait port (trait OrderPort { def place(order: Order): Either[Rejected, Receipt] }), boundary models are case classes, and conversion is a set of total functions (Order.fromLegacy(dto)) possibly written as extension methods; failures are values (Either/Try) rather than exceptions, so the adapter returns the upstream's failure as a typed error. Circe or a derived codec can own the wire half, and opaque types (Scala 3) hide the representation of ids so no raw string crosses the seam. What replaces the classic facade/adapter classes is the trait plus these conversion functions; a facade object is justified when several upstream calls form one domain operation.
pitfalls: Implicit conversions at the seam hide the translation: a given Conversion[LegacyOrder, Order] makes leakage invisible and breaks noisily when the vendor type changes - keep mapping explicit.
Either without a typed error channel degrades to Either[Throwable, A]; define the boundary's own error ADT so callers can match exhaustively.
Case classes compare structurally and expose copy(), so a foreign holder can produce variants the boundary never validated; validate in a smart constructor.
Scala 2/3 cross-building changes the id encoding (opaque types vs tagged types/AnyVal), so the boundary's types need a version-appropriate choice.
